text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-2109 fired for service=redwood-runtime | symptom=tail latency spike (p95 > 1.2s) | severity=P2 | runbook=/runbooks/runtime-latency

raj: acked via PagerDuty. I'm taking this. @ana can you grab logs from the gateways?

anauto: @raj saw this on our canaries too, small % of traffic. popping into logs now. :mag:

luke: seeing a quick burst of 5xx responses from router-proxy-2, maybe connection pool saturation?

raj: interesting — autoscaler shows a short CPU bump on router nodes at the same time. Might be transient spike in requests from a synthetic canary.

incident-bot: Reminder: if PD alert is unacked for 5m escalation to oncall-sre.

anauto: grep snippet: `tail -n 200 /var/log/router-proxy-2.log | grep "upstream reset" | wc -l` -> 78 hits in a 60s window around the spike.

megan: curious if this correlates with the scheduled traffic test from infra? I see a cf job at 15:42 UTC in the jobs dashboard.

luke: yes that job kicked off at ~15:42 and hammered a small subset of endpoints. It should be rate-limited but looks like a misconfigured ramp.

raj: good call. Can we throttle that job or pause it? @megan can you take it down?

megan: pausing the canary job now. `jobsctl pause canary-stress/2026-03-15` -> accepted.

anauto: after pause, 5xxs drop in logs within ~40s. router-proxy-2 5xx rate back to normal.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-2109 auto-resolved (no longer firing). Link: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-2109

raj: confirmed on metrics — tail latency returned to baseline. Looks like noisy synthetic traffic was the trigger, limited to canary cohort (~0.6% of total traffic). No customer-facing impact according to dashboards.

luke: still want to follow up: rate limiter config on that job is too permissive. I'll open a PR to tighten defaults and add a canary throttling guard.

megan: noted — I'll also add a safety sensor to jobsctl to prevent >50 req/s without explicit override.

anauto: quick postmortem notes: cause = misramped synthetic canary; detection = latency SLO alert; mitigation = ack + pause job; impact = none to paying customers; resolution = auto-resolve after traffic stopped.

raj: thanks team. I'll hand over to next rotation — @oncall-rotation you're up for the 18:00 shift, please take over and I can DM a quick summary.

oncall-rotation: thanks @raj — I have the summary and will keep an eye for related regressions.

luke: follow-up actions: 1) PR to jobsctl throttling (link pending) 2) add runbook step to check scheduled jobs dashboard for correlated traffic 3) add a synthetic guard in console.

megan: adding those to the eng-oncall backlog and tagging oncall-sre.

raj: closing thread from my side. If the alert reappears reopen PD and ping here. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Thread closed by raj. Incident duration: ~3m (fired -> auto-resolved). Escalation suppressed due to quick recovery.
